children: Russian mining company Udokan Copper said on Wednesday it had launched copper cathode output at its plant in Russia's far east almost three years after a fire delayed the start of production.
President Vladimir Putin joined the launch ceremony by video link from Vladivostok.
Udokan, Russia's largest copper project, is currently under U.S. sanctions. It began producing copper concentrate in September 2023.

Its operator had planned to launch a hydrometallurgical plant in the second quarter of 2024 to produce up to 135,000 tons of copper per year in the form of either cathodes through the SX-EW process or concentrate. Annual capacity of the first phase of Udokan was expected to rise to 150,000 tons from 2026, with output aimed at both the domestic market and exports to China and other Asian markets.
A fire in December 2023 damaged part of the yet-to-be-launched cathode production facility, although concentrate output was not affected.
Western sanctions imposed on Moscow have complicated imports of mining and processing equipment needed to replace the damaged machinery.
Established in 2008 to develop the Udokan deposit, Udokan Copper is a part of the diversified USM Group, with Russian billionaire Alisher Usmanov being its main shareholder.

Once the second phase of Udokan, previously planned for 2028, is launched, the project is expected to produce around 550,000 tons of copper annually, potentially making it one of the world's five largest copper producers.

title: Russia's Udokan launches copper cathode production after fire-related delay
